Container.Name: Herdr
Container.Overview: Unofficial Unraid image for Herdr (herdr.dev, github.com/herdrdev/herdr), the runtime your coding agents live on: a terminal workspace that keeps Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agents running in a background server, marks each pane working, blocked or idle, and is customised through config.toml and plugins. This container runs Herdr's headless server on your Unraid box behind an SSH server, so you attach from any machine with herdr --remote, or add it as a saved machine, and your agents keep working when you disconnect. The image installs agent CLIs by name, clones your GitHub repositories into a Projects folder, gives the terminals bash, zsh or fish, and works with Unraid's Use Tailscale switch.
Container.Requires: Herdr installed on the machine you attach from, an SSH public key for that machine, and an account or API key for each agent you use.
Container.Changes: ### 2026-11-24 - First release, with Herdr 0.9.5. - The Console signs you in on first use: GitHub by device code, the agents and an SSH key. Run `onboard` to go through it again.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: herdr herder agents claude claude-code codex cursor opencode pi gemini omp terminal tmux multiplexer ssh ai coding headless remote tailscale

Config.Name: SSH port
Config.Description: Port herdr --remote connects to over SSH, as user herdr.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Herdr's config, plugins and saved sessions, SSH host keys, agent logins and shell settings.

Config.Name: Projects
Config.Description: Your repositories, at /projects in the container. Point it at any share.

Config.Name: Authorized keys
Config.Description: SSH public keys allowed to log in as herdr, one per line (the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). Added to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on each start. Password login is off. Or leave it empty and paste a key in the Console, which asks for one on first use.

Config.Name: GitHub token
Config.Description: Optional. A GitHub token git and gh use for cloning, pushing and pull requests. Leave it empty to sign in from the Console instead, which saves the login in the Data folder.

Config.Name: Repositories
Config.Description: Optional. Space-separated owner/name (GitHub) or clone URLs, each cloned once into /projects.

Config.Name: Agents
Config.Description: Space-separated agent CLIs installed once into the Data folder: claude, codex, gemini, omp, opencode, pi, or any npm package name. Log in to each one once from a Herdr pane or the console.

Config.Name: Shell
Config.Description: Shell for Herdr's panes and the console.

Config.Name: Git user name
Config.Description: Optional. Name on the agents' commits.

Config.Name: Git user email
Config.Description: Optional. Email on the agents' commits.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /var/run/docker.sock to let agents create and manage containers. This gives the agents root-level control of this server.

Config.Name: libvirt socket
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /var/run/libvirt/libvirt-sock to let agents start and manage VMs with virsh. This gives the agents root-level control of this server.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the agents run as.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the agents run as.
